_: What each pack in scripts/elections/ reads, and how long its chamber may legally go between two general elections. Read WITHOUT importing the packs (they need npm dependencies; scripts/upstream-liveness.mjs runs with the runtime alone). `name` is stamped on every election row as `up`; `probes` are asked every night by scripts/upstream-liveness.mjs; `terms[].maxGapMonths` is the longest interval the law allows between two general elections of that body, so an index whose newest election is older than that is OVERDUE by a fact about the constitution, not by a guess. Both directions are checked by `node scripts/build-elections.mjs --check`: every pack has an entry here, every entry is a pack, and every body the index carries has a term. docs/ELECTIONS.md §9.

au.name: Australian Electoral Commission · Australian Bureau of Statistics

terms.basis: Constitution s.28 (three years from the first meeting), s.32 and Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 ss.156-159 (writs within 10 days of expiry, polling 33-58 days after the writ; first meeting within 30 days of the return of the writs): 36 months plus at most about six

probes.what: which general elections have an openly licensed return
the 2013 representation order (measured 2026-10-03: 403 to every agent tried)

terms.basis: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms s.4(1): no House continues longer than five years from the return of the writs; Canada Elections Act s.57: polling at least 36 and at most 50 days after the writ
Grundgesetz Art. 39(1): the legislative period is four years, the new election is held 46 to 48 months after it began, and the Bundestag first meets within 30 days of the election

eu.name: European Parliament results service · Eurostat GISCO

probes.what: the results of the current term (the pack walks the terms until one is not served)

terms.basis: Act concerning the election of the members of the European Parliament (1976) Art. 5 and 11: a five-year term, elections in a fixed period in the same weeks of the fifth year

probes.what: the dataset API every round is read through

terms.basis: Code électoral L.O. 121: the Assembly's powers expire after five years; L.O. 122: the general election is held within the sixty days before. A dissolution (Constitution Art. 12) only shortens the gap

hk.name: Registration and Electoral Office · CSDI Portal

terms.basis: Basic Law Art. 69: a four-year term. Observed: the 2020 election was postponed by NPCSC decision to 2021, so this is the law's interval, not a promise the record keeps

jp.name: 総務省 (Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications) · gtfs-gis.jp

terms.basis: 日本国憲法 45条 (任期4年) and 公職選挙法 31条 (任期満了前30日以内に選挙). A dissolution only shortens the gap
日本国憲法 46条 (3年ごとに半数改選) and 公職選挙法 32条 (任期満了前30日以内、国会閉会中に当たれば閉会後24〜30日)

kr.name: National Election Commission (data.nec.go.kr) · OhmyNews constituency maps

probes.why: the pack reads this host over http: measured 2026-10-03, https://data.nec.go.kr gave no answer in 21 s while http answered 200 in 0.5 s

terms.basis: Constitution of the Republic of Korea Art. 42 (a four-year term) and Public Official Election Act Art. 34 (the election is held on the first Wednesday from the 50th day before the term ends)

probes.what: the Central Election Commission — the only publisher of which precinct belongs to which district (measured 2026-09-09 and 2026-10-03: no TCP connection)

terms.basis: Constitution of the Russian Federation Art. 96(1): a five-year term (since 2008); Federal Law 20-FZ Art. 5: the election is called 90-110 days before polling

tw.name: Central Election Commission · Ministry of the Interior (data.gov.tw)

terms.basis: Additional Articles of the Constitution Art. 4: a four-year term; the Civil Servants Election and Recall Act Art. 3 and 6 put the election before the term ends

uk.name: House of Commons Library (psephology) · Office for National Statistics

terms.basis: Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022 s.4: Parliament dissolves five years after it first met; Representation of the People Act 1983 Sch. 1 r.1: polling 25 working days after

us.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab · Jeffrey B. Lewis et al. · us-atlas

terms.basis: U.S. Constitution Art. I §2 (chosen every second year) and 2 U.S.C. §7 (the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of every even-numbered year)
U.S. Constitution Art. I §3 and the Seventeenth Amendment: one third of the Senate every second year, on the same day as the House (2 U.S.C. §1)
a special election is held only when a seat falls vacant (Seventeenth Amendment, cl. 2); no law sets an interval between two of them, so this body is never overdue
